items.evidence: Under "## The bottom line" the overview runs, in order and before "## Scope", "## Decisions this needs from you" and "## Findings": "**1. What FRUS answers directly.** Across the whole printed series — all 553 volumes…", then "**2. Where FRUS points for the rest.** *Series the printed documents came from* (about 5,900 of the 6,700 carry a source note)…", then "**3. What this request cannot get from FRUS.** *\"National security\" as the policymakers' own concept*: I searched the phrase in all 553 volumes…".

No percent sign appears anywhere; every figure names its set or base: "all 553 volumes, of which about 6,700 documents fall under the editors' Cuba headings or name Cuba in their titles"; "about 5,900 of the 6,700 carry a source note"; "about 680 documents carry such citations, none before December 1910"; "It appears in about 1,040 of the Cuba documents, but in only about 47 of them in the officials' own prose"; "the phrase \"Department of State\" was found in all but one of the 553 volumes"; "in no decade do more than 22 Cuba documents use the word"; "Among the Cuba-heavy documents of the 1870s, about half speak of insurrection and about one in three of commerce"; "In the 1940s more than a third of the Cuba documents mention sugar"; "about 114 of every 1,000 documents of the decade name Cuba, and about 72 of every 1,000 sit under a Cuba heading (a quarter of those in one microfiche supplement)"; "Communism or the Soviet Union appears in about three in five of these documents"; "about one in five of the 1960s documents and about half of the 1980 documents (one volume only…)"; "I read 22 documents whole and quote 16 of them."

All 16 documents, in the bottom line and under the findings, carry series, year, volume or part where the volume has one, document number and link, e.g. "Foreign Relations of the United States, 1969–1976, Volume E–11, Part 1, Documents on Mexico; Central America; and the Caribbean, 1973–1976, Document 278, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1969-76ve11p1/d278" and "Papers Relating to the Foreign Relations of the United States, 1873, Part I, Volume II, Document 50, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1873p1v2/d50". The one citation without a document number, "Papers Relating to the Foreign Relations of the United States, 1898, the President's message, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1898/ch83", is an item the digital edition numbers as a chapter, not a document, so series, year, printed heading and link are its fullest form. The short mentions in How this was done ("the 1874 Fish instruction and the 1974 Rush memorandum") and in the Decisions ("The 1902 message of the Cuban President") refer back to documents cited in full elsewhere; no document is cited by a bare id pair or by title alone.

The gaps that are zeros are stated as searches with terms, volumes and controls: "I searched the phrase in all 553 volumes. It appears in about 1,040 of the Cuba documents, but in only about 47 of them in the officials' own prose; in the rest it is the name of an archive or of the Council… Its rate among the 1960s Cuba documents is no higher than in the whole 1960s corpus, so the phrase measures the series, not Cuba. The controls held: the phrase \"Department of State\" was found in all but one of the 553 volumes, and a nonsense term in none." and "*\"Prosperity\"*: in no decade do more than 22 Cuba documents use the word, so it is not how anyone argued." The 1870–1889 gap is stated from the heading census ("the editors filed this in the Spain chapters, and the Cuba headings hold almost nothing for 1870–1889", with the Spain-chapter set of "about 470 Cuba-heavy documents of 1865–1889" in Scope). The last point, "FRUS prints government records. It cannot show what sugar interests, Congress or Cubans thought, except where a document quotes them", is a statement about the series' genre and claims no zero, so no search is owed for it.

The overview holds no SQL, no table or column name and no file path; its only words about the tooling are "I worked from a read-only copy of the FRUS Explorer index covering all 553 volumes", "the index's search folds different words together; for example, it treats \"communism\" and \"communication\" as the same word" and "the app's document-similarity vectors". Strings such as frus1961-63v11/d34 occur only inside the history.state.gov links J3 requires ("https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1961-63v11/d34"), never as a bare id pair. The two "(see the memo)" pointers name a companion document, not a path.

judge:v4.rankingReason: v3: 23 documents and 35 verified quotations across six eras with no gap from 1874 to 1981, a corpus baseline beside every vocabulary count, and the most fully stated "cannot get" searches (terms, sets, what the hits were, a positive and a negative control); dense, but the richest answer a historian receives. v2: a continuous five-era account that holds the 1933–58 sugar hinge and the 1969–70 Soviet-base documents v4 lacks, with every decade count checked against a 300-document random sample of the same decade; weakened by a bottom line that cites most of its documents in shorthand without links, so the historian must scroll to the findings to follow them. v4: the cleanest prose, a self-contained bottom line with every citation linked, controls stated in place, and two findings the others miss (the 1870s slavery argument and the 1974 "no vital interests" memorandum), but it offers no document for 1946–1959 or 1963–1973, the years in which the modern security framing of Cuba formed, and its theme counts other than "national security" have no corpus baseline, so a historian cannot tell a Cuba change from a series-wide one.

score:v4.notes: All four files present (memo.md, overview.md, collection.fruscollection, queries.log), plus scripts s1–s20 with .out files, texts/ (22 bodies) and refuter/checker.out ("16 documents; all checks pass"). Independent verification: coverage row, both controls (552 volumes / 0), the one volume without the control phrase (frus1919Parisv05, 90 rows), apparatus flags of all 6,718 W pairs and all 22 retrieved documents, all 18 quotations as raw substrings, every texts/ body byte-equal to body_text, the frame counts the overview leans on (1870s 57/121/81 of 240; 1960s 1,203/765/437/409/22 of 2,002; 1940s 283 and 161 of 775; 1890s 63 and 82 of 290; 1980s 48 of 89), the mention rates (62.4, 60.1, 17.3, 113.8 per 1,000), eleven lot→NAID resolutions and the two unresolved lots, the decimal-class glosses, the provenance digest across index, binary, map, shards manifest and .generation, the segment decode (314,616 rows; frus1861/d111 at row 110), the two headline Hamming distances (61 and 66) and the random-pair baseline. Vector work was done (Tier-1 binary, centroids, map; no shards), so V1–V6 are scored: V5 and V6 are the clear failures (corpus unclustered share alone; uncalibrated, unlabelled cosines despite a scoreCalibration block in the index). P5 fails on M-08's five numerator-less rates and the bare 28.0%. Caveats recorded inside obeyed verdicts: V1 did not open semantic-shards-manifest.json; V2 did no named known-pair spot check; P6's "11 of 695 series before 1940" has no on-disk source and series-facts holds 698; the overview says "I read 22 documents whole" where M-40 admits keyword-in-context reading; "about 470" rounds 475. The 1945 and 1974 paraphrases in the overview are supported by the retrieved texts. M-47 discloses a stray two-line write to /tmp/x, removed. The overview's URLs carry volume/document ids; these were treated as the citation form, not as id pairs, for O1.
